channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: LIGHT · California Art League
item.description: A live juried exhibition on the theme of Light, presented by the California Art League at bG Gallery in Bergamot Station, Santa Monica, and hung there from 3 to 18 November 2026. Om Navon Bleicher, who founded bG Gallery in 2009 and directs it, is the sole juror and picks both the show and the awards from the digital images submitted. Awards are $800 Best of Show, $500 first place, $200 second place, $100 third place, three honourable mentions and the Theodore Herman Award for Photography. The League - founded in 1948 as the Valley Artists Guild by the sculptor Henry Van Wolf and renamed in 2012 - says painters, sculptors, photographers and collage artists are welcome, and this call accepts drawing, painting, photographs, digital art, mixed media, collage and sculpture; no performance art or AI is accepted. Work must be original and created by the artist from conception to completion, and must not have been shown in a CAL exhibit before. The call is open to CAL members and non-members alike: one or two entries cost $35 for members with dues current and $55 for non-members, the $20 difference being a one-time charge that also gives the new artist a discounted CAL membership; further works are $5 each up to a total of six. There is a 30-inch maximum frame width for wall art. Entries close 11 October at midnight PST and artists are notified on 19 October. Accepted work must be hand delivered to the gallery on 2 November; all work must be for sale and must not be offered for sale anywhere else until 30 days after the show closes, with bG Gallery taking a 50% commission on sales in that period. The opening reception and awards presentation is on Saturday 7 November, with an artists' talk on 15 November and pick-up on 19 November. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $55 non-members / $35 members for 1-2 works, $5 each additional (max 6). Prize: $800 Best of Show + $500/$200/$100 places + Exhibition.

item.title: Palette in Play: How Artists Use Color · Belvedere Tiburon Library
item.description: Juried group exhibition at THE Gallery, the exhibition space of the Belvedere Tiburon Library in Tiburon, California, asking Bay Area artists for the work that best exemplifies how they use colour. The gallery wants submissions that help it “unpack and decode your color choices” — does your use of colour capture feeling, does it manipulate mood, or is your love of colour self-evident? Glowing, vibrant work that shapes perception and muted, calm choices that still the viewer's mind are equally welcome. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, fine art prints, mixed media and textile/fabric art. The show is two-dimensional only, including low-relief work up to five inches deep; sculpture, suspended work and reproductions of your own art in another medium (an offset lithograph of your painting, a giclée of your watercolour) are not considered, and art created using artificial intelligence will not be considered. The library is a family destination and the gallery asks that subject matter suit that audience. THE Gallery blind-juries most of its exhibitions and asks that artist statements omit the artist's name. Selected work hangs 19 November 2026 to 13 January 2027, with an opening reception on 19 November, and is seen by the several thousand visitors who attend gallery and library events or stroll through the library. Entry is $35 for up to three submissions, each of which may carry two additional detail images. All work must be for sale, with 70% to the artist and 30% to THE Gallery; pieces must be ready to hang, between 8 x 10 inches and 72 x 60 inches, and under 50 pounds. Drop-off and pick-up are in person in Tiburon. The prospectus names no cash award — selection into the show is the outcome. — Deadline: October 3, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Flow State · The Aplomb Project
item.description: Juried group exhibition at Aplomb Contemporary Gallery in Dover, New Hampshire, built around Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi's description of flow as “a state in which people are so involved in an activity that nothing else seems to matter”. The gallery is seeking work made in that state of creativity and, in alignment with the mission of its parent non-profit, invites submissions reflecting healing, resilience, identity, transformation, grief, hope, strength or personal perspective. “All interpretations and mediums are welcome”, and the gallery's own calls page names photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture and mixed media. The juror is Marisa Companion, an artist and educator with an MFA from California Institute of the Arts whose work has been featured at the Danforth Museum of Art in Framingham and at Art Basel Miami. Artists may submit one to six works and may apply from any geographic location. Two-dimensional work must arrive securely ready to hang, either framed or gallery-wrapped with painted sides; three-dimensional work in all mediums and multimedia work are also considered. The show runs 6 November to 15 December 2026 with an opening reception on 6 November, and accepted work is due by 3 November. Entry is $35 and the organisers will waive it for artists for whom the fee is a barrier — contact them before applying. Artists retain 60% of sales; The Aplomb Project, a 501(c)(3) that uses art to support people affected by trauma, illness and life transitions, retains a 40% commission and absorbs transaction processing fees. Selected artists ship or deliver their own work, and shipped work must include a prepaid return label or be collected in person. The prospectus names no cash award. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Gomma Photography Grant 2026
item.description: The Gomma Grant returns for its thirteenth edition, run by Gomma Publishing Ltd - the imprint behind Gomma Magazine, publishing since 2004 and, on its own account, having worked with Roger Ballen, Anders Petersen, Michael Ackerman, Momo Okabe, Keizo Kitajima, Araki and Daido Moriyama. The organisers say they look for photographers who develop their own language instead of following trends, and that they judge the work rather than the CV, reputation or number of followers. Entries are welcome across documentary, portrait, landscape, conceptual, black and white, colour, analogue and digital, from a project that may be unfinished, ongoing or completed, and it does not matter how long ago the work was begun. Each entry is 8 to 24 images at 72 dpi, minimum 1,500 pixels on the long edge, with a short description plus an optional artist statement and biography. Multiple entries are allowed provided they come from different bodies of work, and two photographers may submit a collaborative project jointly. The fee depends on which deadline you make: €19 by Friday 25 September, €25 by Thursday 15 October and €35 by the final deadline on Thursday 5 November, with the submission clock set to Hawaii Standard Time (UTC-10). Seven awards are listed. First Prize takes €1,000 and a potential publishing deal with Gomma Publishing and its network; the Gomma New Flavour award takes €300 and the same publishing offer; Second Prize €200 and Third Prize €100; the Honorable Mention, Best Documentary Award and Best Black and White Award carry no cash. Every award adds promotion through Gomma's own channels and media partners, and the organisers say winning work is put to international galleries and curators. AI-generated images are not accepted. No jury is published for this edition - the only answer the FAQ gives on the subject is scoped to 2025, which it says was judged in secret. One conflict worth knowing before you plan around it: the guidelines block says winners are announced in Spring 2027 while the Deadline & Fees block on the same page says February 2027, and the entry form sides with Spring 2027. — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: €19 early bird to Sep 25, €25 to Oct 15, then €35. Prize: €1,000 + €300 + €200 + €100 + possible publication.

item.title: Annual Art For All 2027 · Art Center Waco
item.description: Art Center Waco, a Texas arts centre running since 1973, opens its second Annual Art for All juried exhibition to emerging and established visual artists living in the state of Texas and aged 18 or over. The framing is deliberately wide - the centre's mission is that art is for everyone - and all 2D and 3D media are eligible, with sculpture, painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, mixed media and ceramic fine art named in the prospectus. Read the media rule to its end before ruling yourself out: it says "no digital prints", but the same paragraph clarifies that what is barred is reproductions of original works, giving giclee prints of paintings as the example, "while photographic prints are allowed", and a later hanging clause confirms it by requiring works on paper, photography and collage on paper to be framed and ready to hang. Up to three pieces may be entered for $25, each made within the past five years and not previously shown at Art Center Waco. There is no minimum size and a 72-inch maximum in any direction, with wall works capped at 60lbs; sawtooth hangers, clip frames, keyhole slots, loose eye hooks, adhesives, velcro and command strips are all refused. Three awards go to work in the show - $500 Best of Show, $300 second and $200 third - chosen from the hung exhibition and announced at the opening reception. Selected artists are notified on or before Friday 13 November 2026 and must get their work to the gallery between 1 and 18 December, by drop-off or shipping; shipped work carries a $15 handling fee per box or crate, billed separately after acceptance. Everything hangs in the Beard Gallery at 701 S. 8th Street from 7 January to 5 March 2027, priced for sale with a 30% commission to the centre and 70% to the artist, and the centre says proceeds from sales support both the participating artists and its own exhibitions, education and community programmes. No juror is named for this edition. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $25 (+$15 per shipped box if accepted). Prize: $500 Best of Show + $300 + $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: 19th Annual Open Juried Photographic Exhibit · Cary Photographic Artists
item.description: Cary Photographic Artists, founded in 2007 and described on its own site as the Triangle's only group whose mission is to develop and enhance the practice of photographic art, has run this open juried show every autumn since then. It is a print show: digital files go through CaFE but are not what is judged, and every entry must be printed, mounted, framed and hand-delivered to the Cary Senior Center on Monday 19 October before it is judged - the club's homepage tells photographers who cannot get work to Cary, NC not to enter. About 200 images are typically submitted and 50 are hung. There are two categories, MONOCHROME and COLOR, each with $200, $125 and $75 places and three honourable mentions, plus the Bobbi Hopp Best in Show Award of $400, named for the club's late founder. Any photographic process may be used as long as the photographic process is dominant; canvas wraps and prints on wood, metal, foam core or other surfaces are accepted; framed size cannot exceed 33 inches on the longest edge; work accepted into a prior CPA juried or digital exhibition is not eligible; and the artist's signature must not be visible on the front during judging. No AI or text-to-generative-fill images are accepted, and entrants retain the rights to their images. The jurors are Sarah Shea Roberto, a North Carolina photographer specialising in the silver gelatin darkroom who teaches experimental darkroom techniques at the NC State University Crafts Center, and Stacy Bloom Rexrode, Curator of Exhibitions and Collections with the City of Raleigh. Entry opens on CaFE on 15 September; artists whose images are accepted are telephoned on the evening of 20 October and work that is not selected is collected the next day; the show hangs at the Cary Senior Center from 20 October to 19 December; and a reception with comments by the jurors and presentation of awards is at 6pm on Friday 23 October. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 images). Prize: $400 Best in Show + $200/$125/$75 per category.

item.title: World Sports Photography Awards 2027
item.description: The World Sports Photography Awards, sponsored by Canon, are open for their 2027 edition, free of charge and open to photographers of all ages from any country - the organisers expect mainly professional and semi-professional sports photographers, with some amateurs. Entrants may submit up to ten single images made between December 2025 and November 2026, placed across 24 sporting categories, with no limit on how many categories one photographer enters. Each category produces a top ten - Gold, Silver, Bronze and seven Special Merits - and an overall top three is chosen from the category Gold winners. The organisers say prizes are provided by the awards' sponsors but publish no schedule of them, and this cycle is run entirely online with no in-person awards. Judging is by a panel of ninety named senior figures from sport, media, brands and photography, recused from any category where they have a conflict of interest; they include Tony Duffy, the photographer who founded Allsport, Lee Martin of Getty Images, Justin Feck of The Daily Mail, Andrés Ballesteros of the EFE agency and Jamie Schwaberow of NCAA Photos. The manipulation rules are strict and worth reading before entering: no multiple exposures, polyptychs or stitched panoramas made in software (in-camera versions are accepted), no adding, rearranging, reversing, distorting or removing anything within the frame, cropping and the removal of sensor dust or scan scratches only, and no staging or recreation of events without disclosure in the caption. All entries must be created with a camera; synthetic or AI-generated images are barred and generative fill brings automatic disqualification. Entrants keep copyright and grant a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence for uses connected with the awards, with no payment due for them. Entries opened on 9 September 2026, a shortlist follows in December and the winners are announced on 14 January 2027. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Beyond the Mountains Fund 2026–27 · Tinworks Art
item.description: Beyond the Mountains Fund is Montana's arm of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program, run by Tinworks Art, a non-profit arts organisation in Bozeman; the fund joined the network as a regional partner in 2026. Each year the fund awards one grant of $10,000 and ten grants of $5,000 to Montana-based artists for independent, public-facing projects that encourage experimentation and collaboration, with priority given to Indigenous, emerging and mid-career artists; established artists are eligible when seeking support to explore new, experimental or previously underdeveloped areas of their practice. Projects must take place in Montana, be artist-organised and self-initiated, and operate within a visual arts context the fund defines broadly to include visual art, performance art, digital art and mixed media. They must happen outside a conventional studio or commercial gallery setting, be accessible to the public in community spaces, and charge no admission or participation fee; 501(c)(3) organisations and for-profit businesses cannot apply. One proposal per person per cycle, and past awardees may reapply two years after their award date. The application asks for contact details, an artist bio, a 250-character project summary, a 3,000-character project description and a basic budget, plus information on collaborators, the intended audience or site and any outreach plans; supplementary imagery and sketches are welcome, and timeline and budget templates are provided. Applications are reviewed by a panel of three to five compensated artists and arts professionals with strong ties to the local and regional arts community and expertise in nontraditional, community-centred art practices. Half the award is disbursed up front and half on completion of an interim project report. The 2026 window opened August 1 and closes October 1, 2026 at 11:59pm MT; grantees are announced in December 2026, initial project activities run 1 January to 30 June 2027, an interim report is due 30 June 2027, project activities complete over July–November 2027 and final reports and documentation are due 31 December 2027. Free to apply, through Submittable. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000–$10,000.

item.title: Provision Fund 2026 · Real Art Ways
item.description: The Provision Fund is Connecticut's Andy Warhol Foundation Regional Regranting programme, administered by Real Art Ways in Hartford and running for the first time in 2026. Six $10,000 grants are awarded through a juried open call to artists based in Connecticut, and there is no fee to apply. Projects must be grounded in the visual arts - which the fund defines as broadly as possible, with other disciplines allowed so long as visual art is the driving force - and must have a public-facing component; the guidelines offer publications, living room galleries, garage performance spaces, virtual reality film screenings, community gardens, and oral history and archival projects as examples of what that might look like. Individual artists, artist groups and informal collectives are all eligible and encouraged; applicants must be independent and unincorporated, non-profit organisations cannot apply, work commissioned by museums or universities is ineligible, and funded projects will not take place at Real Art Ways. The lead applicant must live in Connecticut, may not be a full-time student and needs a Social Security number for 1099 reporting, while collaborators may live anywhere. A competitive application must include a line item paying the artists for their labour, and the artists must retain creative and financial control. The application asks for a project title, a 150-word summary, a 500-word narrative, a timeline, a location description of up to 250 words, a budget, five to ten work samples (still images plus up to five video links) and a CV. Three guest jurors - Saya Woolfalk, Seph Rodney and Kelsey Halliday Johnson - assess artistic excellence and clarity of vision, feasibility, the quality of the public-facing component and thoughtful engagement with community, site or social context. Applications opened July 20 and close September 20, 2026 at 11:59pm; awardees are announced in November 2026 and the grant period runs January 15, 2027 to January 15, 2028. Submissions go through Submittable. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000.

item.title: Precipice Fund Round 15 · Portland Institute for Contemporary Art
item.description: Since 2013 the Precipice Fund has supported unincorporated visual art collectives, alternative spaces, artist-run initiatives and collaborative projects in and around Portland, Oregon. It is administered by the Portland Institute for Contemporary Art as part of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program, and from Round 15 additional support from The Ford Family Foundation extends its capacity to invest in artist-run spaces and independent exhibition projects. Round 15 awards grants of $500 to $5,000, $145,000 in total. Projects must be rooted in the visual arts: interdisciplinary work in performance or other media qualifies only where visual art is clearly central, film is eligible during the creation phase but not for post-production or distribution, and sound art is generally eligible where the work sits within an expanded visual art context. Applications must be collaborative, with two to six collaborators and one named Primary Contact - the fund explicitly does not support the work of an individual artist working alone. The Primary Contact must live in the Portland, Oregon metropolitan area and in Oregon; collaborators may live anywhere. Every funded project must include a meaningful public component, may not be the core programming of a 501(c)(3), and may not be submitted through fiscal sponsorship. Grant funds can cover artist fees and collaborator compensation, exhibition production and installation, materials and fabrication, equipment rental, publication and printing, accessibility services, documentation, venue rental, administration, marketing and project-related transport. Applications typically include a project title and description, a project timeline, a statement of artistic intent, a description of public engagement, collaborator information, a project budget, work samples and any supporting materials. Viewing the pre-recorded Round 15 information session is required before applying, and optional 15-minute conversations with staff are offered afterwards. A panel of artists, curators, organisers, writers and other members of the visual arts community reviews all eligible applications through discussion rather than numerical scoring alone, and may award full or partial funding. Applications opened August 10 and close Sunday September 20, 2026 at 11:59pm PDT, with panel review in early November, notification in mid-November, the public announcement in early December and a grant period running January to December 2027. Free to apply, through Submittable. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500–$5,000.

item.title: Interlace Project Grant 2026
item.description: Interlace Project Grants give Providence-based artists $6,000 to make and publicly present new visual work. The fund is Rhode Island's arm of the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts' Regional Regranting Program and is administered by Dirt Palace Public Projects; it exists to make visible often unseen and under-supported artistic activity by artists at all career stages, and to cultivate engaged communities around that work through collaboration in process or presentation. Fundable activities include a new body of visual artwork with a publicly accessible component, a public event, performance or intervention, a site-specific or public-facing art project, a new exhibition or exhibition series, a screening, lecture, broadcast or workshop series, publications in printed or digital form, and experimental forms. The fund will not support projects led by non-profits, incorporated businesses or students, applications made purely to rent studio space or to cover classes, travel or equipment, or large projects for which the grant would cover only a portion of the budget - Interlace expects to be the primary source of funding. Applicants must live within a 10-mile radius of Providence and in the state of Rhode Island (the radius does not extend into Massachusetts), be 18 or over, have been making visual art for at least two years, have resided in Rhode Island for at least the year before the deadline, not be full-time students, and not have completed a Project Grant as lead applicant in the past two years. Applications ask for contact information, visual support materials, a project title, synopsis and biographies, a project description addressing the fund's priorities of visual art, collaboration and engagement, and a budget; a group may apply but must name a lead applicant, who receives the funds and files the final report. An independent panel of national and local artists, curators and arts professionals ranks proposals on originality, clarity of application materials and commitment to those priorities, and the panellists are named when the awardees are announced. Applications opened July 13, an early-review deadline fell on August 16, and the final deadline is Sunday September 13, 2026 at 11:59pm EST; applicants are notified in November 2026 and grantees announced between December 2026 and January 2027. Free to apply, through Submittable. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $6,000.

item.title: 2027 Wedding Cake House Residencies · Dirt Palace
item.description: Dirt Palace, the artist-run space in Providence, Rhode Island, offers short, project-based residencies in the Wedding Cake House with a focus on mid-career artists, and is taking applications for the full suite of its 2027 offerings. Nine sessions are on the calendar, each running a week or a little longer: group residencies from January 12-21, January 28 - February 6 and November 14-22, where artists apply individually or in small groups and are placed in a cohort alongside other artists; a Family Teen residency February 14-20 for artist parents attending with children aged 13-16; a Caregiver group residency March 1-10 for artists who act as caregivers in their personal lives or professions; a Super Duo March 18-27 and Duo residencies April 6-15 and December 6-15 for pairs who apply together, with no requirement that they collaborate; and a Family Youth residency July 25 - August 1 for artists with children aged 8-12 (the info page's own section for that residency says 7-12; the season date list, the application question block and the apply page all say 8-12). There are no fees to apply or to attend and no stipends or travel budgets. Residents are housed; group residencies provide breakfast, lunch and groceries for dinner, with each resident cooking one dinner and helping to prep another, and duo residents get a welcome meal and kitchen access. Everyone also has access to facilities at Dirt Palace Classic, the organisation's original live/work space, including a print shop, a large workroom and a sound rehearsal studio. Days are unstructured, with residents asked to keep errands and outside work to a minimum; group residencies eat together each evening and hold an in-house artist talk, presentation, activity or reading by each resident afterwards, and close with a public component that often takes the form of an open house, open studio, talk, screening or performance. Work made on site has included writing and research, audio mixing and recording, video editing, photography, collage, drawing, sewing and durational performance art. The 2027 call is framed around the line 'No one's coming to save us', and the organisers are looking for artists whose starting point is figuring out how to keep making work that is responsive to this moment. Applications are no longer limited to artists living in New England, though preference goes to artists from New England and Rhode Island in particular; international applications are not accepted this year, and non-artists collaborating with artists may be part of a duo. Applications close October 15, 2026, with applicants notified the week of December 1. Free, through Submittable. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency.

item.title: The Art of Illustration · The Firefly Artists
item.description: The Firefly Artists, an artist cooperative founded in Northport, New York in 2011 and now running a gallery at 90 Main Street, asks for work that tells a story: book covers, movie posters, magazine spreads, comic pages, illustrated passages, political cartoons, articles or poems, with type incorporated or sent separately. Pieces are judged "not only on artistic merit but also how well it tells and sells the story". The framing is illustration-led - the gallery's own calendar heads it "Illustrator Show" - but photography is not a guest here: it is named in the accepted-media list on both the eligibility and the requirements pages ("drawing, painting, photography, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, collage, fabric work, glasswork, jewelry and digital media"), and the gallery's no-reproductions rule carries an explicit carve-out, "No reproductions will be accepted, with the exception of photography and digital art". Editorial, book-cover and photo-illustration work is squarely in scope. Entry is $35 for the first image and $5 for each of up to three more; artists nationwide may apply and there is no age bar. Awards are First Prize $150, Second Prize $75, Third Prize $50 and Honorable Mention, and nothing in the awards block narrows the eligible pool by medium. Work must be original and human-made - AI-generated art is not eligible, nor is anything made under close instruction in a workshop or class. Maximum frame size is 36 inches on the longest side, sculpture no larger than 12 inches in any direction; accepted work must arrive framed, wired and ready to hang, with plexiglass rather than glass on anything 16x20 inches or larger. All work must be for sale and the gallery takes a 35% commission; artists insure their own work while it is on view. Acceptance letters go out 22 October, selected work drops off 1, 4 and 5 November, the show hangs from Saturday 7 November to Sunday 6 December 2026 in the gallery's Darcy Arts Center exhibition space with a reception on Thursday 12 November, and pickup runs 7, 9 and 12 December - after which the gallery charges $5 a day in storage, and work still unclaimed 90 days after the show closes becomes the property of the gallery. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: $35 (first image) + $5 each additional, up to 4. Prize: $150 + $75 + $50.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence — July–November 2027 · Surel's Place
item.description: Surel's Place runs month-long live-work residencies in Garden City, Idaho, in the late artist Surel Mitchell's own home and studio, and it takes applications against two fixed deadlines a year. This is the second of them: 1 March 2027, for residencies beginning roughly four months later. There is no application fee and no residency fee - rent, utilities and wi-fi are covered, and residents receive a living stipend of $100 a week, a $300 travel stipend, the use of the house bicycles, free or discounted tickets to local art events, marketing through the organisation's channels, and logistics and installation help for their public events. Each resident is assigned a host who introduces them to the local arts community, and one residency each cycle includes outreach to local schools through the PARTNER Schools Program. Photography is not in the org's medium list - it names "painters, writers, musicians, architects, filmmakers, and choreographers" - but the governing clause is "any artist who needs a place to focus", and the organisation's own upcoming-artists roster currently lists Eli Craven, October 2026, Photography/Sculpture. The property cannot take loud or messy processes such as welding or blacksmithing, and the org warns that work which is predominantly conceptual may find less enthusiasm with the jury. Residents must live at the house, take no other employment during the stay, give at least one public workshop of two to three hours, present a show or lecture on the residency work, and donate one piece to Surel's Place for future fundraising; the commission on sales arising from a residency is 35% of the retail price, dropping to 15% on merchandise or on work tangential to your medium, such as books. Applicants must be 25 or older and genuine non-smokers - the whole property is non-smoking and the org is blunt about it. Partners may join - no more than two adults, and there may be a surcharge for the extra utilities - but children and pets cannot. Note that the March round is when applications from playwrights and screenwriters reopen after a pause. One thing to confirm with the org before you plan travel: the apply page's deadline table gives this round's window as July to November 2027, while the FAQ and the apply page's own note about literary applicants both say July to December. Visual artists complete the online Artist-in-Residence Application in one sitting - it cannot be saved part-way - and email the accompanying cover letter, proposal including a workshop outline, CV, and 4 to 6 images with an image list by midnight MST on the deadline; the organisation says late applications can be held for the next round. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: 1-month residency + stipends.

item.title: Seeing Sound · New Orleans Photo Alliance
item.description: The New Orleans Photo Alliance - the 501(c)(3) behind the annual PhotoNOLA festival, now in its 21st year, and a gallery on Magazine Street - joins the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Foundation for a show about the long relationship between music and photography: from stages to streets, from full orchestras to solo practice sessions. Entrants are asked to think broadly about form, format, process and approach, and the call is pitched in the spirit of Roy DeCarava's The Sound That I Saw, inviting a wide and improvisational approach to lens-based work about the sound and images that move us, in New Orleans and beyond. The juror is Bruce “Sunpie” Barnes, a New Orleans musician, photographer, author and former National Park Service ranger of thirty years who has played his own Afro-Louisiana music - blues, zydeco, gospel, Caribbean and African influenced rhythms - in more than fifty countries. Submissions are open to all photographers, NOPA membership is not required and all ages are accepted. Fine-art nudes and implied nudes are acceptable and digitally manipulated work is welcome; AI-generated photographs are not permitted. One wrinkle in the prospectus: the written instructions cap entries at five pieces while the CaFE upload form is configured for three to ten images, and the lower written figure is what is stored here. Entry is $35, or $25 for NOPA members, with bundles at $60 (fee plus a new basic membership) and $85 (fee plus a Silver membership including an online portfolio listing). Selected work is dropped off at the NOPA Center, 2011 Magazine Street, or shipped with a return label to NOPA's mailbox service at 3436 Magazine Street #134 - the prospectus warns that packages are not guaranteed at the gallery address; the show opens in late October 2026 and stays up through December and PhotoNOLA Fest. Sales are split 60/40 in the artist's favour and photographers pay shipping. NOPA's own open-calls page still lists earlier 2026 calls, so the organiser-authored CaFE prospectus is currently the only live surface for this edition. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 ($25 NOPA members; $60 or $85 bundled with a new membership). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: CURRENTS 2026 · New Orleans Photo Alliance
item.description: CURRENTS is the annual PhotoNOLA showcase at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art, and the one exhibition the New Orleans Photo Alliance reserves for its own members: eight to ten portfolios chosen to give an overview of contemporary photographic practices and projects, with up to four images hung per selected photographer. Membership is the only gate and it can be bought at the point of entry, with the NOPA team verifying membership before jurying begins. Watch the fee, though: the prospectus text promises members a $25 submission fee and a $60 entry-plus-membership bundle, but the CaFE entry form itself prints a single $35 entry fee with no member rate, and offers membership only as a separate $35 basic or $60 Silver charge - so joining at entry works out at $70 rather than $60. NOPA's other current call on the same portal does show a discounted member row, so the missing discount here looks like a configuration slip worth querying before you pay. The 2026 juror is Bill Boling, a book publisher and the creator of Fall Line Press, who lives and works in Milledgeville, Georgia; he studied photography under Stephen Shore at Bard in the early 2000s and has exhibited at the New Museum in New York and the Window Gallery at the University of Auckland. Entrants submit between four and ten images, JPG, up to 5MB, sized to 1800 pixels on the short side. Photographers accepted into the immediately preceding CURRENTS are asked to sit this one out, and images shown in previous CURRENTS exhibitions cannot be resubmitted - though different images from a previously featured series are eligible. Selected work must arrive framed and ready to hang at the NOPA Center rather than the Ogden, and shipping is the artist's responsibility. The exhibition runs 4 December 2026 to 1 February 2027 during the 21st PhotoNOLA festival. PhotoNOLA's own calls-for-entries page still lists the 2025 edition, so the organiser-authored CaFE prospectus is the live surface for this cycle. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (prospectus text promises members $25; the entry form lists no member rate) + $35 or $60 to join at entry. Prize: Exhibition at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art.

item.title: Joshua Tree Highlands Artist Residency 2027–2028
item.description: JTHAR is an artist-centric nonprofit residency established in 2007 that each year invites six artists from around the world to work in the high desert near the west entrance of Joshua Tree National Park. Three seven-week residencies are on offer for 2027-2028: 4 May to 22 June 2027, 24 August to 12 October 2027, and 11 January to 29 February 2028 - though jthar.org's own summary labels that third window January to March 2028, a month wider than the prospectus, so confirm the winter dates if that is the session you want. Each resident is assigned their own house on five acres of panoramic desert, may work there or in the JTHAR studio - a large space divided by movable walls - and receives a $1,500 scholarship to defray the cost of taking part, spendable on materials, transport or meals. Photography is named outright in the accepted media alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, film, video, new media, installation, fiction and non-fiction writing, interdisciplinary work, social practice and architecture; musical submissions are not being accepted this cycle. Selection is by JTHAR board members and selected jurors on the merit of the portfolio and the residency proposal, with priority to proposals that anticipate transformations and discoveries inspired by place. Visual artists submit a minimum of five images and every applicant submits a project proposal. Three terms worth knowing before applying: residents are required to donate one completed work to the JTHAR program, artists must provide their own transport and need a vehicle for the stay, and the residency cannot accommodate partners, family members or pets - the seven weeks are attended in full, no exceptions. There is a mid-residency review with the board and the option of an open-studio exhibition at the end. Open to US and international artists aged 18 and over; the fee is non-refundable and JTHAR says it cannot waive it, as it funds the residency stipends. Applications open on 15 September 2026 and close 15 December 2026 at 11:59 PM Mountain Time, with selected artists announced on 28 February 2027. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $1,500 scholarship + seven-week residency.

item.title: Art Squared 2026 · Metro Art Studios
item.description: Metro Art Studios is a 501(c)(3) housed in a three-storey renovated corset factory in Bridgeport's South End, with 38 loft studios for professional musicians and visual artists and Crown Gallery on the ground floor. Art Squared is its annual fundraising exhibit, timed to open during the city-wide Bridgeport Art Trail, which brings close to 2,000 visitors through the building over the weekend. Every work is square - a minimum of 10 x 10 inches and a maximum of 14 x 14 inches including any frame - and is priced by the artist at $100, $200 or $300, with a 50% commission retained by Metro and 50% paid to the artist within 30 days of the show closing. All wall-hung fine art media are welcome and photography is named explicitly, alongside painting, printmaking, textiles and mixed media; work must be finished and able to hang on a single nail. There is no entry fee and each artist may submit up to three original works, one image per work. Entries must be entirely the entrant's own and made without an instructor's supervision; copies of existing artworks or work based on others' copyrighted art are not eligible. Open to artists aged 18 and over: the prospectus's eligibility section sets no geographic bar while its summary describes the show as an opportunity for artists of the greater Bridgeport region, and the binding practical constraint is that accepted work must be dropped off in person at Metro Art Studios on 21 October, 1 to 3 pm - the prospectus calls that a Saturday, but 21 October 2026 falls on a Wednesday, so confirm the day with the gallery before you plan the trip. Accepted artists are notified 13 October; the exhibition runs 7 November to 11 December 2026 and unsold work is collected on 12 December. Art is insured while at Metro, with liability for theft or damage limited to 50% of the sale price. Metro's own site currently carries last year's Art Squared entry form, so the CaFE prospectus is the live surface for the 2026 edition. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: On the Rise 2027 · Blue Line Arts
item.description: Blue Line Arts, a nonprofit gallery in Roseville, California celebrating sixty years in 2026, brings back On the Rise, its emerging-artist exhibition for artists aged 14 to 24 at the time of applying. The gallery pitches it as a first gallery show and a first-hand education in how a juried exhibition works from beginning to end, and photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, sculpture and digital art. The entry fee is $25 and covers one to five images, but Blue Line Arts members at the College Student and Artist levels, and high-school students in Placer, Sacramento, El Dorado, Yolo, Yuba, Sutter and Nevada counties, submit for free; 50% discount codes are offered to high-school students outside those areas and to community-college and university students regardless of region. Codes are issued by hand during gallery hours, Tuesday to Saturday, so request one well ahead of the deadline. Note that the gallery calls this a regional exhibition and its eligibility text says artists must reside in qualified regions, while the fee structure explicitly provides for applicants outside those counties and the entry portal lists the call as national - worth an email to the gallery before assuming you are out of range. Work must be original, completed within the last two years, not previously exhibited at Blue Line Arts, and offered for sale; 2-D work must arrive ready to hang. The gallery handles all sales, with non-members receiving a 50% commission and members 60%. Artists under 18 apply through a parent or guardian, who signs the consignment agreement and receives any sale proceeds. Notification is 9 April 2027; the exhibition runs 8 May to 19 June 2027, with an opening reception on 15 May and a closing reception on 19 June. — Deadline: March 12, 2027. Fee: $25 (free for some students and members; 50% discount codes on request). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art Without Borders · LELA International Artists
item.description: LELA International Artists, a Los Angeles 501(c)(3) that has run annual international artist workshops and exhibitions since 1996 and for many years has taken part in the city of Nagasaki's annual 8.9 Peace Exhibition, invites artists and photographers worldwide to Art Without Borders, a virtual international exhibition on the theme of art that crosses borders and connects people across cultures, countries, languages and experiences. There is no set subject: entrants are asked for original work reflecting their own experience, imagination, culture, environment, identity or vision of an interconnected world. Photography is named in the accepted-media list alongside drawing, painting, mixed media, collage, printmaking, fiber art, digital art and sculpture. Up to three works per artist; entry is $45, or $35 for LELA members, paid through EntryThingy. Betty Ann Brown, PhD - art historian, critic and curator, professor of art history at California State University Northridge since 1986 and a past president of the boards of both the Los Angeles Woman's Building and the Southern California Women's Caucus for Art - is the sole juror and also selects the awards: $300 first, $200 second, $100 third and up to four honorable mentions. Work created under an instructor's direct supervision is not eligible, and no AI-generated artwork is accepted. Selected work stays online for the run of the show and afterwards in the archived-exhibitions pages indefinitely. Artists may offer work for sale and deal directly with buyers; LELA takes no commission. The exhibition is web-only, opening with a Zoom event on 6 November 2026 and running to 1 January 2027. Note that the organiser prints two schedules: an Important Dates block partway down the entry form still reads Thursday 1 October with a 2 November opening, while the form's own header, the EntryThingy deadline panel and LELA's own events page all give 10 October and a 6 November opening - the later set is the one the entry portal enforces. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: $45 ($35 members) for up to 3 works. Prize: $300 / $200 / $100 + 4 honorable mentions.

item.title: Winter Member Show 2027 · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Maryland Federation of Art's winter members' exhibition at Circle Gallery in Annapolis, running 6-30 January 2027. Any original 2D or 3D work will be considered and every entry is blind juried; this year's juror has not yet been named. Cash awards total $700 - $500 designated by the juror, a $100 Conley Award restricted to 3D work chosen by Susi and Rob Conley, and a $100 Friends of the Arts award - so a photographer competes for $600 of the pool rather than all of it. Entry is open to MFA members residing in any state or territory of the US, Canada or Mexico; non-members join first (basic membership is $70 a year) and then enter at the member rate. Up to six original works made in the past three years may be entered, nothing larger than 72 inches in any direction, and work previously exhibited at Circle Gallery is not eligible; video is accepted as a link plus a still frame. Artists are notified 3 December 2026 at 5 PM, accepted and shipped work arrives 27-30 December, and there is a virtual awards ceremony on opening day and an in-person reception at Circle Gallery on the closing day, 30 January. Members retain 75% of sales. MFA's General Guidelines, which the terms of entry incorporate, regulate photographic prints directly and bar work created via image-generative AI. Founded in 1963, MFA is a 501(c)(3) non-profit supported by the Maryland State Arts Council. — Deadline: November 4, 2026. Fee: $30/2 works + $4.50 each addl. Prize: $700 + exhibition.

item.title: 22nd Annual Wabi-Sabi · O'Hanlon Center for the Arts
item.description: O'Hanlon Center for the Arts, a non-profit in Mill Valley, California, invites work for the 22nd edition of its annual Wabi-Sabi exhibition, on view 20 October - 19 November 2026. Wabi-sabi finds beauty in the simple, rustic and unassuming - in things unfinished, irregular, weathered or worn by time - and the call asks for work that is dynamic, spontaneous, irregular and poetic rather than perfected: a rusty object, a found fragment, a rough surface, an unexpected combination of natural materials. Contemporary, exploratory and experimental entries are encouraged. Sherrie Lovler and Colin Talcroft jury. Open to all artists aged 16 and over, two works each. This is an in-gallery show and there are no digital submissions: the registration form is completed online in advance and the work itself must be hand-delivered to 616 Throckmorton Avenue on Friday 9 October, 11 am - 4 pm, or Saturday 10 October, 10 am - 1 pm. Wall-hung pieces are capped at 40 inches wide and, on the registration form, 60 inches tall. Entry is $40, or $30 for Artist-level OHCA members, and taking out a new Artist-level membership at drop-off waives the fee. Jury results are emailed by 5 pm on Wednesday 14 October; there is an art talk and opening reception on Saturday 31 October and a First Tuesday Art Walk reception on 3 November. Work previously shown at O'Hanlon is not eligible, and artists agree to donate 30% of any sale made in the exhibition's first 60 days. The call names no accepted-media list and neither do the gallery policies; photography sits squarely in the centre's programme, which has included a dedicated photography show juried by SFMOMA's Shana Lopes and recurring Wabi Sabi photography workshops. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: $40 ($30 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Studios Inc Residency 2027
item.description: Studios Inc, a non-profit arts organisation and gallery in the Crossroads Arts District of Kansas City, Missouri, awards a three-year studio residency to mid-career artists. The term runs February 2027 to January 2030 and gives residents an industrial studio of 500–3,000 sq ft, access to a wood shop and a fenced outdoor lot for installation work, a solo exhibition in the organisation's large exhibition hall, inclusion in the annual Spring exhibition, and studio visits through the Studios Patron Program. Applicants must be mid-career — at least seven years of practice since undergraduate study or the professional equivalent, with a developed body of work recognised regionally or nationally — and must already live in the Greater Kansas City area or be willing to relocate there for the three years, including a short statement of intent to relocate if applying from elsewhere. Applications run August 1 to October 1, 2026 (midnight US-CDT) through Submittable, with a $35 fee; the jury reviews in October, finalists present in November and awards are announced mid-December 2026. Residents provide their own materials and must carry public liability and property damage insurance. Past residents include the photographers Elijah Gowin, Patty Carroll and Jaimie Warren, and the photo-collage artist Miki Baird. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Three-year studio space + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Sustainable Darkroom Futures Residency
item.description: The Sustainable Darkroom is seeking five UK-based artists to propose research and development projects for innovative, sustainable systems in photography. Each resident receives a £3,400 grant across two instalments, bi-weekly online seminars with speakers including Renata Marques Leitão, Rob Hopkins, Tim Crossland and Dominic Wilcox, bi-weekly online mentorship with project-specific development, and access to facilities and technical support at the University of Sunderland for testing and prototyping. The six-month hybrid programme culminates in an exhibition and symposium in Sunderland in October 2027, with a travel stipend and accommodation, plus inclusion in an online publication of the final research documents. The organisers ask applicants to “think beyond the established norms in this sector” and to envision “radical, unorthodox, even outlandish ideas” about photographic systems — material, philosophical, political, legal or structural — and say outright they are not seeking submissions on already well-established processes such as plant-based developers or botanical cyanotype toning. Prototypes, blueprints, test images and written papers all count as outcomes. Two of the five places are reserved for residents of Northern England (South Yorkshire to the Scottish Borders) and two for artists with disabilities; applicants may fulfil both criteria. Audio and video applications up to 10 minutes are welcome. Run in partnership with the Northern Centre of Photography and the University of Sunderland research group Bridging Photographies, Cultures, Communities, and supported by Arts Council England and The Grocers’ Charity. Online Q&A sessions on 23 September and 11 October. Free to enter; open to UK residents only. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed 2–9 December 2026. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £3,400 grant + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Midnight & Moss · Gallery 40
item.description: Gallery 40, the contemporary gallery in the 1915 atrium at 40 Cannon Street in Poughkeepsie, is looking for work that explores “the mysterious beauty of the night through a palette where green and blue take center stage” — the stillness of a forest after dark, moonlight through leaves, reflections on dark water. Green and blue should be the predominant elements; other colours may be incorporated but the visual language should stay anchored in the two hues. Painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, mixed media, textiles and other contemporary practices are all encouraged, limited to 2-dimensional wall work no larger than 36 inches wide by 48 inches high framed, professionally presented and wired to hang. Juror Nansi Lent — a Hudson Valley painter who founded the Poughkeepsie gallery Womenswork.art and has served on the board of the National Association of Women Artists — selects the show and awards a single $100 Best in Show. The exhibition runs 5 December 2026 to 3 January 2027 with an opening reception on Saturday 5 December, 5–7pm. Open to artists 18 and over living in the United States; up to three works for one $35 fee. No nudes, no reproduction prints, and no work previously exhibited at Gallery 40. All work must be for sale, with the gallery retaining a 40% commission and the artist setting the retail price. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: $100 Best in Show.

item.title: Xposure International Photography Awards 2026/27
item.description: Xposure's International Photography Awards recognise outstanding photography from across the world, celebrating work that demonstrates originality, narrative depth and technical excellence. The awards are free to enter and open to photographers at all stages of their careers, and are presented within the wider Xposure programme in Sharjah, where shortlisted and winning work is introduced to international audiences through exhibition, publication and professional engagement during the festival's annual gathering of photographers, editors, curators and industry leaders. The organiser describes nine categories spanning contemporary practice, among them Architectural Photography, Nature & Landscape, Night Photography, Portraiture, Sports Photography, Street Photography, Mobile Photography and Photo-manipulation & AI; entries may be single images or cohesive series. You may enter up to ten images or films per user distributed in any ratio across the categories, only one image may be uploaded at a time, and work must have been taken or produced in the past three years. Each entry carries a title, caption and place taken, and all entry information must be submitted in English. Judging runs in three stages: a first round scoring individual submissions for visual strength and originality, a second round assessing composition, technical execution and coherence in a series, and a final collective deliberation that names category winners, runners-up and an Overall Winner. There are seven nominees per category. The Overall Winner receives USD 6,000, flights and accommodation to the awards ceremony in Sharjah and inclusion in the Xposure festival exhibition; each Category Winner receives USD 3,000 with the same travel and exhibition, each Category Runner-up USD 1,500 with travel and exhibition, and nominees receive an online exhibition and an image displayed during the festival. Beyond a category specifically designed for photo manipulation, entries must not add or remove content or stage a photograph to mislead the viewer, though adjustments of levels, colour, contrast and brightness are permitted; watermarks or names that are not part of the original capture are disqualifying, and nominated finalists must supply high-resolution TIFF and RAW files for verification. Entrants to the AI & Creative Expression category must have exercised primary creative control and must retain prompts, revisions, seeds, model and version information or layered working files as evidence of authorship. Entry is open to all nationalities over 18; there is a separate Junior category for UAE residents under 18. A separate Visual Storytelling Award runs alongside for six-image stories. An entrant cannot hold a cash placing in more than one Xposure programme in the same festival year, with the Independent and Freelance Photojournalist Award taking precedence over these awards. Xposure is the Sharjah platform for photography, filmmaking and visual storytelling, powered by the Sharjah Government Media Bureau. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $6,000 + $3,000 per category + Exhibition.

item.title: Seeing Red — Annual Color Theme Show · Harrison Center
item.description: Each year the Harrison Center invites submissions that celebrate interpretations of an annual colour theme for a December group exhibition in its Harrison Gallery and Gallery Annex; for 2026 the theme is Seeing Red. Presented by the Katharine B. Sutphin Foundation, the exhibition celebrates all interpretations of the colour red, and the organiser encourages entrants to push the boundaries of creative inspiration - naming the warmth and compositional balance of Matisse's The Dessert: Harmony in Red, the colour's symbolism of luck and celebration in Eastern traditions, and political undercurrents from Delacroix to Soviet constructivist typography as starting points. Work must incorporate the colour red, but the approach may be cultural, emotional, historical or deeply personal. Entry is free and the Harrison Center states it accepts work from artists of all skill levels and backgrounds, across all varieties of media; the application repeats that all media are accepted, with video entrants supplying their own projection equipment and artists installing anything that is not easily hung. Only one piece may be submitted per entry - no diptychs or triptychs unless framed together, and a small series is not a single-piece submission - and the submitted image must show a finished work rather than a concept. Applicants must state in the submission whether a piece is AI-generated or AI-assisted, and the Harrison Center retains the right to decline artwork based on appropriateness for all audiences. Cash prizes from the Katharine B. Sutphin Foundation are announced by the judges at 7pm on opening night; the application lists Best in Show $5,000, First Place $3,500, Second Place $2,500, Third Place $200 and Honorable Mentions of $300 each, while the Harrison Center's own page summarises the awards as cash prizes from $250 to $5,000. Selected artists are notified by Friday, November 13th 2026. All work in the show must be for sale and the Harrison Center takes a 30% commission, which also applies for 30 days after the show closes to sales resulting from it. Accepted work is delivered to the City Gallery at 15th and N Delaware St, wired and ready to hang (no sawtooth hangers), with early drop-off on November 23rd and 24th and a final drop-off by noon on Monday November 30th. The exhibition opens Friday, December 4th from 6pm to 9pm and hangs through the month of December. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000 Best in Show + cash awards.

item.title: Stories and Traditions — Native American Art Exhibition · Montpelier Arts Center
item.description: Stories and Traditions is an exhibition highlighting artwork by Native American artists in the Mid-Atlantic area of Maryland, Virginia, DC and Pennsylvania, which the organiser notes may include the indigenous peoples of the Piscataway, Lumbee, Pamunkey, Mattaponi, Chickahominy, Nanticoke and Pocomoke. The brief asks what the stories and traditions of native peoples are as the seasons shift into Fall (Harvest) and Winter (Storytelling and Reflection), a time much of the nation spends observing commercialised holidays. Artists of Native American descent are invited to apply through paintings, drawings, sculpture and fiber as well as traditional artisan crafts such as ceramics, beading and jewellery, and the call's accepted-media list also names photography and video alongside those. Entry is free, each artist may submit up to six works, and image, video, audio and PDF files are all accepted. The exhibition runs November 10th 2026 to January 3rd 2027 with a free public reception on Sunday, December 13th from 2 to 4pm. Montpelier Arts Center is a public arts venue in Laurel, Maryland, run by the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission's Parks and Recreation department in Prince George's County; its building holds galleries, gas- and electric-fired kilns, a digital lab, printmaking presses and classrooms, admission is free, and the centre runs a year-round exhibition programme alongside its Artists on the Rise juried teen exhibition, a Main Gallery call for proposals and a Library Gallery competition for Maryland artists. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Braiding Indigeneity · Der Greif
item.description: Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, invites photographers, artists and visual storytellers to revisit how images construct identity, land and relational memory. The call was developed within Der Greif's online exhibitions series and grounds itself in the ethos of Issue 19, "I Am, Because of You, Mother Earth", guest-edited by Zanele Muholi, carrying that relational ethic forward in conversation with Indigenous visual sovereignties. The organisers are looking for creatives engaging with indigeneity through genuine collaboration, consent, and accountability to the Indigenous individuals, knowledge-holders, or communities whose ways of framing life and relationality inform the work; the title pays tribute to Robin Wall Kimmerer's Braiding Sweetgrass, a reading that inspired the call's take. Submissions are one project of up to 10 images, cohesive and not previously featured by Der Greif. Selected participants join a hybrid workshop - online and in person in Paris on 14 November 2026, three hours, time and location to be announced - integrated into the FUTURES Hub programme, with collaborative image analysis, reciprocal critique and public auditory sessions; the selected work is then shown in an online exhibition in November. Twelve to sixteen artists are selected. The call is open to photographers internationally, particularly emerging and mid-career artists, with no age or regional restrictions, and the eligibility line says only that it is preferable to be available for the Paris workshop - but the call page carries a firmer note in bold before submitting: you must already be in Paris on 14 November 2026 to apply, as Der Greif cannot compensate travel or accommodation costs. Der Greif describes the 15 EUR as a voluntary donation, while its Picter entry page renders a flat 15 EUR charge; artists unable to contribute financially can email voucher-special@dergreif.org for a 50% or 100% discount code. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: €15 (waivers available). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Open Juried Photography Show 2026 · Hull Artists Association
item.description: Hull Artists' Open Juried Photography Show runs from Friday 9 October to Wednesday 18 November at the Nantasket Beach Resort, a hotel across the street from Nantasket Beach on the Massachusetts coast that the association describes as a tourist and business destination with excellent exposure for the show. The exhibit is non-themed and open to photographers of all ages; membership in Hull Artists Association is not required for entry, though members receive discounted entry fees and a better commission split - 70% to the artist against 60% for non-members. Work is judged in two categories: Black-and-White Photography, which includes any monochromatic hue such as sepia, cyan and brown as well as neutral greys, and Color Photography. Each category awards First Place $100, Second Place $75 and Third Place $50, each with a ribbon, plus ribbons for honourable mentions. The juror is Bobbi Lane. Every piece displayed must be original and derived from the artist's own photograph; the association allows enhancement in programs such as Photoshop and Lightroom, but AI-generated images, stock images and clip art are not allowed, in part or in full. Artists may enter up to six pieces for the juror's consideration, though no more than two per artist can be accepted. Maximum artwork size is 41 inches on the longest side including frame, all work must be for sale with the price entered before checkout, and given the venue setting all work must be PG and family-friendly. Accepted work must be hand-delivered: Hull Artists cannot receive or accept shipped art. Entry is $10 plus $10 per piece for members and $15 plus $10 per piece for non-members, so one piece costs $20 or $25 and six cost $70 or $75. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $20 members / $25 non-members for one piece, plus $10 per additional piece. Prize: $100 / $75 / $50 in each of two categories.

item.title: Off the Wall 2026 · ARTS Southeast
item.description: Since 2015 ARTS Southeast's affordable small works exhibition has been an annual tradition in Savannah's Starland District, presenting eclectic, collectible work by members of the local arts community. Off the Wall is a salon-style show of small works in all media in which pieces can be taken directly off the wall after purchase, so locals and out-of-town visitors can bring home or gift their purchases right away; running through the holiday gifting season, this year's edition will evolve over the course of its run into the new year, with works added to the wall as other works sell. Artists may submit up to four images for consideration and will be notified of first-round acceptances; those whose work sells may be invited to display more, and the organisers encourage multiples, iterative works and series. ARTS Southeast takes no commission on sales - patrons are directed to contact artists directly and artists receive 100% of the sale price, with the 501(c)(3) noting only that a 30% donation would be greatly appreciated - and promotes selected work through its website, social media, a press release and its newsletter. Every piece must be for sale at a retail price between $25 and $300 and must be 30 inches or less in every direction; work may be in any medium, framing is not required and alternative presentations of 2D work are welcome, but framed pieces should arrive wired and ready to hang with D-rings rather than sawtooth hangers. The call is open to current ARTS Southeast Supporters, a membership bought outright with tiers starting at $25 (Student Supporter) and $50 (Artist Supporter). The show is on display 22 October 2026 to 16 January 2027 with an opening reception on Friday 6 November, artwork drop-off 15-18 October during gallery hours and pickup on 17 January 2027; the gallery is closed to the public from 13 December 2026 to 13 January 2027. — Deadline: October 10, 2026. Fee: Free (ARTS Southeast Supporter membership required, from $25). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Independent & Freelance Photojournalist Award 2026 · Xposure
item.description: The Independent and Freelance Photojournalist Award recognises excellence in independent visual reporting across three categories - Spot News, Environment and Solutions - with one Category Winner each, and Xposure stresses that recognition is strictly category specific, with no aggregated ranking across categories. Each Category Winner receives a USD 5,000 cash prize, an exhibition at the annual Xposure festival in Sharjah and finalist recognition; each category also awards one Category Runner Up an official certificate and an online presentation of the awarded essay. Entrants may submit one 12-image photo essay per category, addressing urgent, underreported or impactful global issues. All photographs must be original and taken within the past 24 months, and essays submitted previously in the same form may not be resubmitted. The award is open to individuals aged 18 or older regardless of nationality, but participants must hold a valid national or international press card issued by a recognised association, or provide evidence of published journalistic work and a supporting reference from a recognised media bureau; a scan of the press pass is uploaded at registration and every application is verified by a moderator before an account is created. Freelance photojournalists not in full-time employment by a media outlet are eligible. The ethical bar is explicit - images must present an accurate and honest account of events without manipulation, alteration or distortion, standard adjustments to exposure, colour, contrast and brightness are permitted, watermarks, names or added elements are disqualifying, and entries using AI-generated images are not permitted. Entrants retain full copyright and grant Xposure non-exclusive rights to use winning and nominated images to promote the festival and the award. Xposure is the Sharjah platform for photography, filmmaking and visual storytelling, powered by the Sharjah Government Media Bureau; entering the award does not exclude you from also entering the Xposure International Photography & Film Awards or the Global Focus Project, though a participant cannot hold a cash placing in more than one Xposure programme in the same festival year, and IFPA results take precedence. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3 × $5,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Group Book — Connectedness · Pomegranate Press
item.description: Pomegranate Press is an independent publishing house based in New York City - once Richmond, Virginia - which has since 2015 specialised in showcasing contemporary photography and other mediums of visual art through limited-edition, affordable publications and ephemera. For the first time in three years the press is hosting an open call for photographs to be included in a new, expansive group book, and it expects to accept approximately fifty people. The loose theme is Connectedness, and photographers are asked to send three to six photographs in any relation to that idea; you may include as much or as little about yourself and the work as you like. There is no fee to submit. Submissions go by email to pommesubmissions@gmail.com with the subject line '(Your Name) Group Book Submission'; the press asks that images not be sent as expiring links and encourages low-resolution files, since the press is overseeing every submission itself. Submissions are open until 14 September 2026, with accepted photographers notified by mid-October at the latest, and the book is due out in early 2027. The three previous Pomegranate group books were Playfulness, Nothing Left but Healing, and You, Me, and the Moments; the Playfulness volume, made with Balam, ran to 116 pages at 8 by 10 inches, Swiss bound with embossed back-cover text, in a first edition of 500 copies printed in Argentina and featuring around seventy photographers. The press frames this call as a response to print and publication becoming harder to access, hoping the space will give emerging artists an outlet. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Marni Jenkins Visual Art Prize 2026 · CALYX Press
item.description: CALYX Press, the oldest feminist press in the United States, has launched the inaugural Marni Jenkins Visual Art Prize, a blind competition with a rotating final judge for work by women and nonbinary artists. The winner receives a $400 cash prize and publication in an upcoming issue of CALYX, A Journal of Art and Literature by Women+, the press's biannual print publication, whose every issue carries a glossy full-colour insert of visual art. The winner and up to two runners-up are published on calyxpress.org and receive a complimentary one-volume subscription of three issues - though the press's own contest page words this more broadly, saying the winner and all finalists get the subscription and the website publication. This year's final judge is Betty LaDuke, an Ashland, Oregon painter whose shaped and painted wood panels address social justice, food security and cultural diversity, and whose work is held by the Portland Art Museum, the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art, the Hallie Ford Museum of Art and the Oregon State Capitol. The prize is named for Meredith 'Marni' Jenkins, a founding member of CALYX Press and an accomplished photographer and painter, and it exists to encourage bold new visual art that challenges convention and explores the broad experiences and perspectives of women and nonbinary artists. The submission window runs 1 July to 30 November 2026. Submit up to six pieces of visual art; photographs of three-dimensional work such as sculpture and textile pieces are welcome, and the CALYX editorial collective reads everything first before sending twenty finalists to the judge. Files must be JPG or PNG, at least 300 dpi and at least five inches wide at that resolution, in RGB or CMYK. Work must be unpublished, and simultaneous submissions are discouraged. CALYX operates a strict anti-AI policy and asks that no work generated with AI tools be submitted. Entry is through Submittable at $15, which the press's own page itemises as a $14 consideration fee plus a $1 PayPal processing fee. Winners are announced in January 2027. Note that CALYX also takes free year-round art submissions on a separate track, considered by its Art Collective each May and December. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $400 + Publication.

item.title: SOLO 2027 · Bromfield Gallery
item.description: Bromfield Gallery, founded in 1975 and one of Boston's oldest artist-run galleries, runs SOLO as an annual competition awarding two solo exhibitions with all gallery expenses paid. It is aimed squarely at artists who have not yet had a solo show in a commercial gallery anywhere - group shows, university galleries, libraries, frame shops, cafes and community centres do not disqualify - and all media are welcome. The 2027 juror is Shey Rivera Ríos, Artistic Director of the Boston Center for the Arts, an interdisciplinary artist, cultural worker and curator with a fifteen-year record in arts and community development who serves on the Arts Policy Committee for Grantmakers in the Arts. Entry is $35 for five JPEGs, ideally a recent coherent body of work representing the exhibition you would mount. Finalists are asked to bring three to five pieces of current work to the gallery in October for review by the juror, all entrants are emailed the result, and winners are posted on the gallery website by 1 December. The two winning exhibitions are held in January 2027. The gallery pays the exhibition costs - postcard, exhibition fee, reception and so on - while artists remain responsible for making their work and for travel or shipping; all work in the exhibition must be for sale. Eligibility is limited to the six New England states, Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Vermont, and your primary residence must be in New England from the application deadline through 31 January, the end of the exhibition period. Applications are accepted only through Submittable. Bromfield is in Boston's SoWa district at 450 Harrison Avenue, alongside two dozen contemporary galleries and the Boston Center for the Arts. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Flourish Fund 2026–27 · CultureSource
item.description: The Flourish Fund is CultureSource's regranting programme for Southeast Michigan, run in partnership with the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts as part of its Regional Regranting Program. It awards six grants of $10,000 each, every year, to artist-organised projects that are experimental and risk-taking, collaborative, shared with the public, and rooted in a visual arts practice. Projects can be interdisciplinary but must have a strong foundation in the visual arts, and the fund states that proposals may span mediums and disciplines from sculpture to projection mapping, printmaking to immersive technology, and beyond; recent grantees include a Detroit community-archiving project built on pop-up digitisation events for family photographs and home movies, paired with contemporary artists' work in galleries and installations. Applicants must be independent, unincorporated artists at any career stage, and the lead organiser must live in one of the seven Southeast Michigan counties - Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw, Monroe, Livingston or St Clair - with the project taking place and being publicly shared in one of them. Groups and collectives may apply with a single lead applicant, who receives the funds. Projects run by incorporated entities including LLCs and 501(c)(3)s, by universities, schools, religious institutions or municipalities, or led by currently enrolled high school or university students, are not eligible, and the fund does not support retroactive or reimbursement requests. The application asks for artist and project information, work samples, a proposed budget and several short answers, and is free to enter through Submittable. Applications opened on 13 August and close on Friday 11 September 2026; note that the portal stays open until 11.59pm but technical assistance ends at 5pm. An independent committee including previous Flourish Fund grantees reviews and ranks proposals, then meets to agree the six awards, with notification to all applicants in mid-October. Grantees receive $6,000 on signing and $3,000 at the interim report stage. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000.

item.title: Lightning Fund 2027 · Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions
item.description: LACE, Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions, has opened the seventh edition of its Lightning Fund, an annual regranting programme supported by the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts. This cycle it awards ten artist project grants of $6,000 each to artists and artist-run collectives, projects and publications in Los Angeles County. The same application also decides the Jacki Apple Award, a $10,000 grant to one LA-based mid- or advanced-career artist for work resulting in a performance, media project, exhibition or publication within a year; no separate application is needed. LACE describes its definition of visual art practice as expansive, listing drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, installation and similar mediums alongside film and video, new media, sound art, performance art and social practice; practices firmly rooted in dance, theatre, music or industry, feature and documentary filmmaking are not eligible, nor are nonprofit organisations and LLCs set up for commercial enterprise. Applicants must live in Los Angeles County, be at least 18, and not be currently enrolled in a college programme. Proposals should be innovative and socially relevant and accessible to the public outside traditional museum or gallery settings, and the review prioritises presentations in Los Angeles County; awarded projects are not intended to be shown at LACE. Previous winners may reapply after waiting two cycles. The application asks for contact details, a 300-word account of your practice and past projects, and a 500-word project description covering timeline, collaborators, materials, location and needs, a budget breakdown and one to three work samples. Entry is free, through Submittable. Applications opened on 12 August and close on 23 September 2026 at 11.59pm PST, a deadline LACE describes as firm; decisions and funds follow by the end of January 2027.
